characterList.description: A man with a shaved head and a large beard. He is wearing a blue-and-red plaid shirt and a blue lanyard.
characterList.name: Alexander Bard

content_metadata.description: Alexander Bard's presentation on the impact of the internet and futurism.

qAndA.answer: He stated that the audience tripled in size by the end of his talk.
qAndA.question: What did Alexander Bard mention about the audience size during his presentation?

qAndA.answer: He recommends ebooks over physical books, suggesting they are more convenient to read on devices like iPads.
qAndA.question: What type of book format does Alexander Bard recommend and why?

qAndA.answer: He describes the internet as a new 'layer' over the planet, blending the physical and virtual realms.
qAndA.question: What visual metaphor does Alexander Bard use to describe the internet's impact on the world?

qAndA.answer: He uses the term 'schizophrenic,' highlighting the fragmented and multi-faceted nature of individual identity online.
qAndA.question: What term does Alexander Bard use to describe the new type of human being emerging in the internet age?

qAndA.answer: He provocatively suggests that younger generations should 'give up' on trying to explain the internet age to their parents, implying a significant generational gap in understanding.
qAndA.question: What advice does Alexander Bard give to younger generations regarding their parents?

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: Hello, I'm Alec Sandabard. I'm 51 years old. I live in Stockholm, Sweden. I write mad
books like this and I love all the composers of the world. The presentation here at the
campus part in Berlin was wonderful. There were three times more people in the audience
when I finished than they were when I started, which I think is a good grade. It's horrible
to have a full audience when you start and everybody's left when you finish. So it was
just an exact opposite. I had a very engaged audience, some of them are sitting here, and
we're now continuing after my speech and moving to dialogue mode, which I love because I love
the fact that I can go to conference, give a speech, and then I can talk to people afterwards
that improve my theories even more. So my next speech can be even better. So I try to
practice what I preach. I try to be an interactive human being. So what I talked about today is
the the the Fitturic trilogy, which just came out in the US. And it's the finally all three
books that I've written with John Sertekis have been translated to English. The Fitturic
trilogy consists of three books. One is called the Netacrats, one is called the Global Empire,
one is called the Body Machines. You can buy them separately or you can buy them as one, and I would
recommend the e-books and not the paper books like this old fashioned paper book. The more
comfortable to have an iPad than to have as a paper book. But anyway, the Netacrats is a book
that deals with the ongoing technological revolution, which is of course at the internet,
as a technology. And what it does to us and how we have to rewrite history, and we have to rewrite
the idea what it means to be human being. Because this is the fourth main revolution in human
history and it completely changes everything. So that's the theme of the Netacrats. The Global
Empire is a book that deals with how our worldview has to change. We had a concept of what it meant
to be living in a world before. Of course, physics has changed that completely over the last 100
years. We now realize that there's an enormous universe out there to begin with. They're very tiny
little creatures within this big universe. But the internet even more affects us in this way.
We even think of the world today both as a physical world and as a virtual world at the same time
and they operate together. So we go from the physical experience to the virtual experience, then we
go from the virtual experience back to the physical experience. So the internet is like a new layer
over the planet. And if you combine that layer, which we call the net, with the physical world as
it is, then you get what we call the global empire. And that's why the book is called the global
empire. And it has a lot of theories on that. What's going to happen to politics, what's going to
happen to religion, what's going to happen to metaphysics, what's going to happen to a lot of
different things because of this revolution. And the third book is the one directed to the reader,
him or herself, and this book called the Body Machines. And it deals with how the concept of being a
human being changes completely. We study all the philosophers that have discussed existentialism
before we study Nietzsche, we started Heidegger, all the best thinkers of the previous paradigm.
And then we compared them to this homo-interactive us, this new creature now that steps out, we see
Davidial much more than an individual. It's a very schizophrenic type of being. That has a lot of
different personalities that lives most the online. And then in a secondary world which is physical,
it's a complementary world to the online world. And this of course is a very, very different
human being from the human being that the character or even Nietzsche or Heidegger discussed.
So we need a new philosophy, a new ontology, a new phenomenology, a new understanding of what
it means to be human being. And we open up that discussion with that book, the Body Machines.
I think the most important aspect of the campus party is not speech, it's like mine, the most
important aspect is people meeting. And I think the networking effects of everything we do today
is always the driving force of everything. I don't know, I don't know if people,
a couple of zeros are really conscious of the fact that going to Berlin to meet a lot of people.
But the fact is you meet your old friends and you meet new friends and you expand your friendships
and you expand your connections, you expand your own networks. And that encourages the more creative
and to be co-created with others because creativity in the internet age is not about you
isolating yourself coming up with a brand new idea. That's not going to happen. The way new ideas
are being developed today is that you see yourself as one building block within a bigger system of
people. And together with your friends you create your own community, your own subculture,
and that community becomes creative. So you are co-created, you're creating with others.
And this process of creativity is constant, it's fluid, it just runs on and on and on and never stops.
You can constantly redevelop and change things. If you use terms from the music industry,
you would say that you're constantly remixing everything. Everything is being remixed and remixed
and the new version is being put out all the time with new partners being involved and changing
things. And we love this process. It is very human. It maybe it's more original when it comes to
creativity than the idea of the isolated genius was, the hotel in the franchise. I think it's a
completely dead idea. Anything from factory owners, copyright holders to even fashion designers
are dead now. The idea of the fashion designer is dead because we're all designing our own
fashion now. We design them, we walk into closed store. By our behavior we design the next generation
of clothes. So all the old patriots are dying, all these old artists are dying. And the idea
of life as a work of art is now a co-creative communal process where we participate with others.
The message is that I am a 51 year old guy and I'm trying to understand what's going on in your 23
year old heads. But I can tell you one thing, your parents get nothing. They don't understand
anything what's going on in your life, in your head, in your life world. Your life world is so
alien, so completely different there. Don't even talk to them anymore. They don't get it. They don't
get it. Just give up on them. Just let them die and take over the world. That's what I would
recommend you to do composites.
